data.cultural_impact: Eranna holds cultural significance as a strong and grounding name, rooted in Hindu mythology. It represents a deep connection to nature, symbolizing stability, strength, and resilience. In some regions of India, it is also a common name for children born during agricultural seasons, as the earth is believed to be especially nurturing during these times.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Eranna is a powerful name, representing a deep connection to the divine energies of the earth and the mother goddess. In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is often depicted as a restorative and transformative force, rooted in the earth and transforming all experiences into spiritual growth. Eranna thus embodies the qualities of Lord Shiva, imparting strength, resilience, and a deep connection to the divine within.

historical_references.reference: Eranna was a Jaina Tirthankara of the 12th nayakas or Tirthankaras in the present half of the 24 Tirthankaras cycle.
